settings.title: Settings
settings.auto_start_hint: Off by default. WireGuide's background helper runs only while the app is open — automation rules apply during that time. Turn this on to have WireGuide start with your session.
settings.compact_list_hint: Denser rows — hides the endpoint line and shrinks row height so more tunnels fit without scrolling.
settings.kill_switch_hint: Blocks all traffic if VPN drops. Applied automatically on connect.
settings.dns_protection_hint: Blocks DNS to any server except the connected tunnels' resolvers. Tunnels using split DNS (~domain) or no DNS keep system DNS and are not affected. Applied automatically on connect.
settings.health_check_hint: Monitors handshake age and triggers a reconnect if the tunnel looks dead for 180 s. It can also fire after sleep/wake or on an idle tunnel without PersistentKeepalive — keep PersistentKeepalive = 25 set if you use this.
settings.pin_interface_hint: Pins VPN bypass routes to the active network interface. Prevents latency spikes when WiFi and Ethernet are both connected.
settings.about_desc: An open-source VPN client built around WireGuard — drop a config and you're online. A kill switch that doesn't leak, DNS protection that doesn't dodge, and Wi-Fi rules that pick the right tunnel on networks you trust. No command line. No telemetry. No upsell.
settings.about_credits: Built with WireGuard®, Wails, and Svelte.
settings.auto_update_check_hint: When on, WireGuide checks GitHub once a day (with jitter and conditional GETs so it never wastes the public API quota).
settings.notify_auto_hint: Show a notification when a tunnel connects or disconnects without you doing it here (Automation rules, the command line, wake from sleep) and when the helper reports a problem.
settings.update_check_failing: Update check failing: {n} in a row, last attempt {when}.
settings.dns_protection_blocking: Active: all DNS is blocked except local resolvers.
settings.dns_protection_inactive: Not applied — split DNS or no DNS
settings.helper_old: This helper predates detailed status. Use Repair helper to update it.
settings.helper_repair_hint: Reinstalls WireGuide's background helper. This is the only action here that asks for your administrator password.
settings.helper_repair_confirm: This reinstalls the helper and asks for administrator permission. WireGuide explains why before the prompt appears.
settings.helper_repair_connected: Disconnect all tunnels first: repairing the helper would drop them.
settings.reset_title: Reset DNS & firewall to system defaults
settings.reset_desc: Removes WireGuide's firewall rules and split-DNS entries and restores DNS from the saved pre-VPN state. Use it if DNS or the network is stuck after a crash. Your settings are not changed.
settings.reset_confirm: This removes all WireGuide firewall rules and DNS overrides and flushes the DNS cache.
settings.reset_confirm_connected: A tunnel is connected. Resetting disconnects it first, then removes all WireGuide firewall rules and DNS overrides.
settings.reset_refused: A tunnel is still connected, so nothing was changed.
settings.reset_step_kill_switch: Kill switch: the setting stays on and is applied again the next time a tunnel connects
settings.helper_reason_launchd_socket: launchd started the helper because a client connected to its socket
settings.helper_reason_legacy: launchd did not hand over a socket; the helper listens on its own
settings.dns_protection_idle: Turned on. Nothing to protect until a tunnel with DNS servers connects.
settings.export_diagnostics_hint: Saves a zip with logs, redacted tunnel configs, DNS, routes and firewall state for bug reports. Private and preshared keys are never included.

tools.dns_leak_desc: Checks how this computer resolves names while a tunnel is connected. With a global DNS tunnel, queries should go to the tunnel's servers instead of your ISP's; any other resolver is a leak. With a split DNS tunnel (~domain entries), only the listed domains go to the tunnel's resolver and everything else keeps using your normal DNS, so other resolvers are expected.
tools.dns_leak_split: Split DNS active: only the listed domains use the tunnel resolver
tools.dns_leak_split_failed: Split DNS check failed: the tunnel resolver is not registered for all listed domains
tools.route_desc: Shows where your network traffic is going. Routes marked VPN flow through the tunnel; others go directly to the internet.
tools.dns_leak_dig_note: Terminal tip: dig and nslookup bypass split-DNS resolvers, so private names can fail there even when the tunnel works. Use dscacheutil -q host -a name <name> or ping instead.
tools.dns_leak_linux_note: Terminal tip: use resolvectl query <name> to see which resolver answers a name.
tools.route_skipped_hint: AllowedIPs range skipped because it overlaps your LAN

wifi_permission.title: Location Services required
wifi_permission.desc: Wi-Fi auto-connect rules need access to your current network name. Grant permission in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services.

automation.title: Automation
automation.hint: Rules run top to bottom; the first matching condition wins. Pick a condition and type its value, or use the suggestion for the network you're on. "This network" matches a specific router by its gateway MAC (precise; tells apart networks that share a subnet); "subnet" matches an IP range. Add separate rules to connect and to disconnect. "is not" matches only when the value is known and different: while it is unknown (for example a blank Wi-Fi name while roaming, or the network just changed and hasn't settled for about 15 seconds) the tunnel is left alone and later rules are not tried.
automation.empty: No rules — this tunnel is never auto-managed. Add a rule below.
automation.drag_hint: drag to reorder — the topmost matching rule wins
automation.mac_invalid: not a valid MAC address (e.g. b0:38:6c:54:8b:ab)
automation.negated_hint: "is not" matches only when the value is known and different; while unknown the tunnel is left as it is.

why.title: Automation status
why.net_unknown: Wi-Fi name unknown — Location Services may be off; "is not" rules hold
why.net_type_unknown: Network type unknown; "is not" rules hold
why.settling: settling, {n} s ("is not" rules on hold)
why.v_held: on hold — waiting for the network to settle or the Wi-Fi name to be known
why.v_paused_connected: paused — you connected it by hand; resumes when the network changes
why.v_paused_disconnected: paused — you disconnected it by hand; resumes when the network changes
why.v_overlap: not connecting — {cidr} overlaps your current LAN
why.v_no_match: no rule matches the current network

ping_health.title: Reconnect on ping failure
ping_health.description: Reconnect this tunnel when every target fails for the chosen number of consecutive checks. A reply from any target keeps the connection active.
ping_health.targets_hint: Up to 5 IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, one per line. Use hosts that reply to ICMP inside this tunnel’s AllowedIPs.
ping_health.cooldown: Each check waits up to 3 seconds. Monitoring starts after one interval; reconnect attempts are at least 60 seconds apart. This setting is independent of handshake health checks.

verify.title: Verify
verify.note: Read-only checks that run only when you click. Nothing runs automatically.
verify.hint_handshake_none: The peer has not answered. Check the endpoint, keys and firewall.
verify.hint_handshake_old: Idle tunnels only re-handshake when traffic flows or PersistentKeepalive is set.
verify.hint_route_overlap: The local network wins for this prefix, so peers there are not reached through the tunnel.
verify.hint_route_missing: The route was not installed. Try reconnecting the tunnel.
verify.hint_route_other: Another interface or VPN owns this prefix.
verify.hint_resolver_missing: macOS did not register the resolver. Try reconnecting the tunnel.
verify.hint_resolver_outside: Add the resolver address to AllowedIPs so queries travel through the tunnel.
verify.hint_ping_failed: The host is down, filtered, or not routed through the tunnel.
verify.hint_resolve_nxdomain: The resolver answered but does not know this name. Check the ~domain and the resolver.
verify.hint_resolve_timeout: No answer in time. The resolver may be unreachable through the tunnel.
verify.hint_resolve_failed: The name did not resolve. Check the resolver and routes.
verify.detail_route_unmanaged: Routes are not managed by WireGuide (Table = {table})
verify.detail_resolver_unsupported: Split DNS is not checked on this platform
verify.detail_resolver_scutil_failed: Could not read the DNS configuration ({err})
verify.detail_resolver_outside: ~{domain} -> {resolver}: resolver reached over the local network, not the tunnel
verify.detail_resolve_outside: {name} -> {addrs} ({ms} ms) via {resolver}: resolver reached over the local network, not the tunnel
verify.hint_route_unmanaged: Table is set, so WireGuide installs no routes in the main table. Add them yourself.

lint.dns_global_outside: {servers} is reached over your normal network, not the tunnel, and will replace your system DNS on every interface while connected (DNS protection will then allow only this server). Add ~domain to scope it, or remove DNS.
lint.dns_mdns: ~{domain} overlaps with mDNS (.local); lookups may not reach the tunnel's DNS server. Prefer a different suffix such as .lan or .corp.
lint.dns_split_windows: Split DNS (~domain) is not supported on Windows; this tunnel's DNS settings are ignored and system DNS is used.
lint.mtu_missing: MTU is not set (auto). If connections stall on large transfers, try MTU = 1420 or lower.
lint.mtu_high: MTU {mtu} is above {max} and may fragment packets over typical 1500-byte paths.
lint.dns_lan_none: No private-name resolution: add DNS = {gateway}, ~<domain> to resolve names on the remote network.
lint.dns_no_reverse: Split DNS has no reverse zone, so IP-to-name lookups for the remote network use system DNS. Add {zones} to resolve them through the tunnel.
lint.cmp_tilde_info: Route only this domain (and its subdomains) to the tunnel's DNS server. All other queries keep using your system DNS. Needs at least one DNS server IP in the same line.
lint.cmp_template_info: Server, one split domain and its reverse zone. Replace corp.lan with your private domain.
lint.hover_global: DNS = 1.1.1.1 replaces the system DNS on every interface while connected.
lint.hover_split: DNS = 10.0.0.1, ~corp.lan sends only corp.lan queries to the tunnel's server and leaves system DNS alone.
lint.hover_none: No DNS line leaves system DNS untouched, so private names will not resolve through the tunnel.
lint.hover_nxdomain: A name that the tunnel's server does not know returns NXDOMAIN; there is no fallback to system DNS.
lint.hover_dig: dig bypasses split DNS and queries servers directly; use dscacheutil -q host -a name <name> to test what apps see.
lint.hover_match: Split DNS: queries for {domain} and its subdomains go to this tunnel's DNS server; everything else uses system DNS.

preview.dns_global: Replaces DNS on all network services with {servers}.
preview.dns_split: Adds {servers} as a resolver for {domains} only. Your system DNS is unchanged.
preview.dns_split_unsupported: Split DNS is not supported here, so DNS is left unchanged and {domains} will not resolve through the tunnel.
preview.dns_search: Changes the system search domains to {domains}. No DNS servers change.
preview.routes_full: Sends all your traffic through the tunnel.
preview.routes_skipped: Skips {ranges}: it overlaps your local network, so it stays local.
